decisions.question: The Contracts section lists topic-model@v1 as produces. This phase delivers its behavior guarantees (G4, G7 to G9, G11, G13 to G15, G17 to G21, G23, G24) and its gate replays the contract unrestricted, while the declarations and the type-level guarantees (G1 to G3, G5, G6, G10, G12, G16, G22, G25 to G27) landed in nidana.model.3. How much of the contract's text goes inline, and does the Validation section's behavior bullet (which names the guarantees the behavior cases cover) come with it?

options.label: Interface and Guarantees whole
options.consequence: Both bodies verbatim and untruncated, as nidana.model.3 had them (351 lines of Interface, 27 guarantees), with the Delivery paragraph that names this phase as the one that delivers every behavior guarantee. The plan writer reads the lineage, equality and redaction rules next to the declarations that already exist and has the type-level guarantees the replay still checks. Costs a long context (668 lines).

options.label: Interface whole, only the delivered guarantees
options.consequence: A shorter Guarantees block (15 of 27), but a selection I would author, which Rule 1 forbids, and the unrestricted replay checks all 27 guarantees, so the plan writer would not see 12 of the rules the gate enforces.

options.label: Add the Validation section
options.consequence: Puts the behavior bullet (which guarantees the cases cover) inline, but the skill's Contracts template excerpts the Interface and Guarantees only; adding a third body is a template change.

decisions.why: The skill's Contracts template names exactly those two bodies (Interface and Guarantees), Rule 1 forbids a selection of my own and Rule 4 forbids truncation, and nidana.model.3 (S105) and nidana.model.5 (S114) did the same. What is new is only that the phase delivers behavior: the Delivery paragraph, inline in the Interface, states it, and the Scope names each guarantee by id. I checked that the Scope covers every guarantee the behavior suite still fails: the topic-model@v1 binding run alone on the committed tree (9 passed, 32 failed, the count hsdd/verify/nidana.model.6.verification.md records) fails G4, G7, G8, G9, G11, G13, G14, G15, G17, G18, G19, G20, G21, G23 and G24, every one named in the Scope, while G6, G10 and G27 already pass; so nothing the Validation bullet lists is missing from the file's reachable text. A skill wording that made the Contracts excerpt depend on what the phase delivers would have changed my mind.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md (Interface, Delivery paragraph; Guarantees; Validation, behavior bullet)

decisions.question: The self-contained gate (Rule 2: 'Every contract, ADR and OQ id the file names has its text inline in its section. Other phases' ids appear only in the Phase block's Dependencies and Collides with lines') flags ids that occur only inside verbatim excerpts, and the impl-gate prints its warning for eight contract ids. decisions.chosen: Apply the gate to ids the file selects; excerpt-internal citations stay as the source's words
decisions.why: Same reasoning as S98, S102, S105, S117 and S120: the Contracts and Open questions selection rules and Rule 1 cannot all hold under a reading of Rule 2 that counts every id inside a mandated excerpt. The phase block's Verification names Spec section 2.4's worked examples, which are in the committed conformance library (hsdd/contract/fixture/topic-model/behavior/topic_model_conformance.dart) and in G19's text, not ids Rule 2 reaches. A skill wording that scoped Rule 2 to selected ids, or told the writer to inline cited contracts, would have changed my mind.
